Assign cells to clones by their likelihood under the clone states

Source: R/clones_assign.R
assign_cells.Rd

Per cell and clone k: the sum over pieces of the depth term ll_depth_shift(z, c_k * log2(cn / 2) / pmax(sd_null, sd_floor), tpar) and the allele term ll_allelic(nA, n, 0.5 + a_k * (f_state - 0.5), rho, two_sided = FALSE) on the cell's votes oriented by clone k's pseudobulk (leave-one-out for k's members). The depth z is taken relative to the reference cells' mean log2 ratio of each piece (ref_cells; removes the shared per-region bias of the normalisation). With mixtures, every pair of clones is also scored as a mixture (weights mix_w; copy numbers mixed; per piece the votes oriented by the pair's clone that is imbalanced there, as for the single clones, with the other clone's haplotype agreement taken from its pooled counts under that orientation). Posterior over singles (prior prior, default uniform) and mixtures (total prior mix_prior); the reported posterior is the best clone's posterior among the single clones.

Usage

assign_cells(
  feat_pieces,
  clones,
  segments,
  tpar,
  rho,
  par = NULL,
  prior = NULL,
  mixtures = TRUE,
  min_post = 0.9,
  mix_prior = 0.05,
  ref_cells = NULL,
  mix_w = 0.5,
  mix_margin = 10,
  mix_rel = 0.1,
  params = caller_defaults(),
  mix_pairs = NULL,
  mult_prior = NULL,
  trunks = NULL,
  max_mix_prior = 0.5
)

Arguments

feat_pieces

list(features = per-cell depth features on the pieces (region_features()), pieces = regions table, votes, atoms, cells = names in vote index order)

clones

data.table cell, clone: the clone members used for orientation (confident singlets)

segments

segments table

tpar

depth null t parameters (fit_depth_null()) or NULL (Gaussian)

rho

per-cell beta-binomial overdispersion

par

data.table clone, c, a (from fit_clone_states()); default c = a = 1

prior

named clone prior (NULL = uniform; a size-proportional prior lets large diffuse clones absorb low-depth cells)

mixtures

score pairwise 50:50 mixtures

min_post

posterior needed for assigned

mix_prior

total prior of the mixture hypotheses

ref_cells

reference cells for the depth centring (NULL = none); the clone states must be relative to the same reference (clone_profiles() ref_cells)

mix_w

mixture weights of the first clone of a pair (0.5 = 50:50; e.g. c(1/3, 1/2, 2/3) for unequal nuclei)

mix_margin

a cell is doublet_like when the mixtures' posterior is > 0.5 and the best mixture beats the best single clone by more than this (log-likelihood)

mix_rel

... and by more than this fraction of the cell's best single-clone log-likelihood ratio (deep cells fit any single clone less perfectly in absolute terms)

params

caller_defaults()

mix_pairs

optional 2-column matrix of the clone pairs scored as mixtures (default all pairs); caller_tumour() passes the pairs whose states differ allelically on >= mix_min_dist bp (clone_state_distance()): a mixture of near-identical (sibling) clones fits a cell between them better than either clone, which is not evidence of a doublet

mult_prior

optional named per-cell multiplet prior probability (e.g. a soft multiplet score): the cell's total mixture prior is max(mix_prior, prior), capped at max_mix_prior

trunks

optional named clone -> trunk vector (clone_trunks()): adds trunk and p_trunk (posterior summed over the clones of the best clone's trunk)

max_mix_prior

cap of the per-cell mixture prior

Value

data.table cell, clone (the likelihood-best single clone, for every cell), posterior, ll_margin, doublet_like, pair, ref_pool, p_mix, ll_mix_gain, ll_best, mix_prior, assigned / confident (posterior >= min_post and not doublet-like) (plus trunk, p_trunk when trunks is given; attribute ll: cells x hypotheses log-likelihood matrix)

Details

The hypotheses are the clones with members plus the fixed normal clone N0 whenever segments has it (caller_tumour() normal_hypothesis), even when no cell is labelled N0 yet: its state is all-neutral, so it needs no orientation, and without it normal cells would be forced into a tumour clone. Its c is the median c of par (attenuation 1) when par has no N0 row.
